selected_instance.why: Natural advance widths match the reference almost exactly at the measured cap heights: Rose 134.3 vs 134 (error 0.002) and Damascena 273.2 vs 281 (error 0.028), needing only +0.97 px positive tracking per gap. Positive tracking cannot cause collisions. No distortion of any kind is required.
selected_instance.rejected_A: wght 300 too narrow — Rose error 0.044, Damascena 0.077
selected_instance.rejected_C: wght 500 too wide — Rose error 0.049, and it would need NEGATIVE tracking

headline_finding: Imbue at opsz 100 / wght 400 is a natural width match for both words without any horizontal scaling, per-glyph forcing or colliding tracking. This is the first candidate in the whole workstream to meet the composition targets by construction rather than by distortion.
what_failed: My outline-conversion step is defective. The Qu2CuPen recording handler only accepted curveTo calls carrying exactly three points, so every call emitting more was silently dropped. The emitted glyphs are fragments — o came out with 4 nodes and c with 3, which is far too few for real outlines — and the raster proof shows shards rather than letterforms. The font is not at fault; the converter is.
next_step: Fix the pen handler to accept multi-segment curveTo, re-run conversion, then validate and inspect. The acquisition, licence provenance and instance selection above all stand and do not need repeating.
